currentContext.expansion: Gratex's FY26 expansion was confined to printing-technology upgrades rather than a new plant. Under technology absorption the Directors' Report records that the Company "added a new 10-colors digital printing machine from EPSON, a world-renowned manufacturer", together with a new print head for the digital printer, a new 6 KVA UPS inverter with batteries for the new printer, 16 batteries for the UPS inverter serving the HP digital printer, and an Apple Mac Mini with a 12TB hard disk for the NAS box. Management states that "Being 10 colors, the digital printing machine gives more vibrancy to our product range. It significantly enhancing our production capacity." The MD&A dates the addition to January 2026 and describes it as the Company's fourth machine overall, saying it "will not only boost turnover but also increase margins in the coming year". The purchase was debt-funded: the current borrowings note records a Profectus Capital Ltd facility described as "Rs 1504500 loan taken tiwards puchase of new printer. Repayable in 48 monthly equal installment of Rs. 40725/- starting from Feb'26. Rate of interest is 13.50% p.a.", secured by a first charge over fixed assets by way of hypothecation of plant & machinery (existing & future). Alongside the addition, the Company wound down its modular furniture & profile (MFP) line, which recorded NIL sales in FY26, and says all operational focus will consolidate into Digital Wallpaper and Catalogue manufacturing, with improved digital wallpaper manufacturing infrastructure opening an export push in FY 2026-27. No expenditure was incurred on research and development, no technology was imported in the last three years, and no steps were taken on conservation of energy (reported NIL).

risks.risk: Input cost volatility in base substrates
risks.note: Listed first among the MD&A's Threats: 'Unpredictable costs for base substrates severely threaten profit margins.' With a net profit margin of 2.58% and an operating profit margin of 3.84% in FY26, a small move in substrate cost is enough to erase profitability.

risks.risk: Cheap Chinese imports eroding price and quality perception
risks.note: The MD&A states that the 'Inflow of cheap Chinese imports continues to erode margins and disrupt quality perception in the market' - a structural pricing ceiling on a domestically produced, undifferentiated decorative print product.

'Currency volatility has escalated import costs, requiring proactive procurement and pricing strategies.' The Company reports NIL export earnings and NIL formal imports on CIF basis, so it carries FX cost exposure through domestic pricing of imported inputs without any natural export hedge.

risks.risk: Extreme single-customer and related-party revenue concentration
risks.note: The credit-risk note in the financial-statements section (carried in the sibling profile bundle, not in this one) records that 'The company has very high concentration of credit risk to a single customer which is a related party' and the geographic-information note shows total revenue from customers is essentially all revenue generated from related parties, namely Marshalls Enterprises India Pvt. Ltd. - an enterprise over which KMP exercise significant influence. Loss or repricing of this single counterparty would remove nearly the whole revenue base, and receivables from it ballooned during FY26 (current ratio fell from 7.36 to 4.23).

risks.risk: Sub-scale operations in a conservative market
risks.note: Management itself flags this: 'The Company being a small-cap company and the conservative market in which it operates is a cause of concern from the point of view of operating profits to the Company.' Total FY26 sales were Rs. 4.27 crores - a scale at which fixed costs and a single machine outage are material.

risks.risk: Narrowed revenue base after exiting modular furniture, with two declining service lines
risks.note: The MFP (Modular Furniture & Profile) line recorded NIL sales in FY26 against Rs. 47.29 Lakhs a year earlier, and the ratio note attributes the variance to 'The company has discontinued its one of the segment of the business of furniture which affected overall efficiency of business'. All operational focus now consolidates into Digital Wallpaper and Catalogue manufacturing, while warehousing income fell 10% and franchisee commission income also declined - so growth rests on one product line.

risks.risk: Export ambition is unproven and conditional on global conditions
risks.note: The FY27 turnover target of 25% leans on an export push that so far consists of leads from a single first-time exhibition at Frankfurt in January 2026; management is only 'hopeful that once the current global turmoil settles, we will be able to derive good orders from the world market'. The Company recorded NIL FOB value of exports in both FY26 and FY25.

risks.risk: Reduced external governance oversight given size thresholds
risks.note: The Directors' Report states that a Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27 of SEBI LODR 'is not applicable to the Company as it does not fall under the criteria of Paid up Share Capital of Rs. 10 Crore and Turnover of Rs. 25 Crores', and the Company is not required to submit an Annual Secretarial Compliance Report to the stock exchange. Combined with the related-party-dominated revenue model, this leaves fewer external checks on the arm's-length assertion.

risks.risk: New secured borrowing against a previously near-debt-free balance sheet
risks.note: The ratio note records that 'The company has taken a new loan which has resulted in variation for DSCR as well as debt equity ratio'; DSCR fell from 5.02 to 1.85 and the debt-equity ratio rose from 0.01 to 0.04. The printer facility is secured by a first charge over plant & machinery, existing and future, which encumbers the asset base against future funding needs.
